qs.q:
Technology and the family — Which person says…

A=Alan (children don't play outside anymore, only screens; no social skills; disrespect for elders)
B=Brian (machines help with household tasks; microwave, dishwasher = more free time; grandmother washed clothes all day)
C=Catherine (families can stay in touch via technology; BUT wonders if they pay attention or just wait for pings)
D=David (washing machines, phones great; home entertainment keeps families together; BUT obesity and no outdoor play; overall positive)
E=Esther (life changed quickly, still in shock; families must learn to control technology use; will get better with time)
F=Fiona (loves TV, YouTube, gaming; risky cyberspace; cyber-bullying; adults must adapt to this new 'jungle')

0. the more we get used to it, the more technology will benefit us? [E=Esther]
1. domestic life was more demanding before technology?
2. children no longer respect adults?
3. families must be more disciplined in how they use technology?
4. life is more interesting because of technology?
5. they are not sure whether technology is good for us or not?
6. technology is bad for health?
7. technology saves time?
8. that because of technology families communicate less?
9. technology provides families with more opportunities to do things together?
10. we don't understand technology yet?
11. there are more advantages than disadvantages in technology?
12. young people may become an easy target when using technology?
items: 1 — domestic life was more demanding before technology?
3 — families must be more disciplined in how they use technology?
4 — life is more interesting because of technology?
5 — they are not sure whether technology is good for us or not?
8 — that because of technology families communicate less?
9 — technology provides families with more opportunities to do things together?
11 — there are more advantages than disadvantages in technology?
12 — young people may become an easy target when using technology?

qs.q:
Musical ability

"They would always quote Mrs Mallory: 'That boy is TONE DEAF.'"

The writer didn't learn to play an instrument when he was young because…
A his parents couldn't afford it.
B he didn't work hard enough at school.
C his parents didn't think him musically gifted.
D he never bothered to do so.
opts: he didn't work hard enough at school.
his parents didn't think him musically gifted.
he never bothered to do so.

qs.q:
Musical ability

"The term was widely talked about by people who had NO IDEA OF ITS TRUE MEANING."

The writer says that tone deafness…
A was used as an excuse by lazy music teachers.
B was misunderstood by the general public.
C was a condition that affected many people.
D was a condition inherited from parents.
opts: was used as an excuse by lazy music teachers.
was misunderstood by the general public.
was a condition that affected many people.
was a condition inherited from parents.

qs.q:
In an age of robots, schools are teaching our children to be redundant

"Children love learning when allowed to apply their natural creativity and curiosity. They learn to walk, talk, eat and play spontaneously, by watching and experimenting. (19) ____. We sit them down, force-feed them with useless facts."

A For example, the Essa academy in Bolton gives every pupil an iPad.
B Its programme got rid of traditional subjects in favour of the students' explorations of themes.
C One of them, the Mantle of the Expert, encourages them to form teams of inquiry.
D Is it surprising when children, bursting with energy, are confined to the spot like battery chickens?
E Their skills are not only redundant but counter-productive.
F When they get to school, we suppress this instinct.
G The less autonomy they are granted, the more they are blamed for the failures of the system.
H Had they set out to ensure that children find learning difficult, they could not have done a better job.
opts: A — The Essa academy gives every pupil an iPad.
B — Got rid of traditional subjects in favour of explorations.
C — Mantle of the Expert encourages teams of inquiry.
D — Is it surprising when children bursting with energy are confined like battery chickens?
E — Their skills are not only redundant but counter-productive.
F — When they get to school, we suppress this instinct.
G — The less autonomy they are granted, the more they are blamed.
H — Had they set out to ensure children find learning difficult, they could not have done a better job.
